title: Optimal Euclidean error for pure-DP statistical-query release
formal: Does there exist a universal C>0 such that, for every integers n,T,k≥1, every real ε∈(0,1], and every k functions f_j:[T]→[−1,1], there is a pure ε-differentially private mechanism M with E[‖M(x)−f(x)‖₂]/√k≤C·min{1,√(ln(2T)/(εn))} for every x∈[T]^n?
context:

definitions: [T]={1,…,T}; the database is an ordered list x=(x₁,…,x_n). Write f(x)_j=(1/n)Σ_i f_j(x_i). The queries and ε are fixed before accessing x. A mechanism is a family of Borel probability distributions M_x on ℝ^k indexed by all databases x; it may depend on n,T,k,ε and the whole query family. Pure ε-differential privacy means M_x(E)≤exp(ε)M_y(E) for every Borel set E⊆ℝ^k and every two databases differing in at most one position by replacement. The privacy requirement includes every database, without a distributional promise. In the error bound a random output is drawn from M_x and the expectation is over this output alone. ‖z‖₂=(Σ_j z_j²)^(1/2). The answer is an existence question about probability kernels, with no computational or finite-precision requirement. C is independent of all parameters and queries. The normalization is expected Euclidean norm divided by √k, rather than a maximum-coordinate bound or the square root of expected squared error. The source’s log T target has the equivalent harmless truncation and T=1 convention written here.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.

sentences: A statistical query averages a bounded function over a private database, and answering many such queries produces a vector of estimates.

The saved proposal asks for pure differential privacy with normalized Euclidean error at most a constant times min{1, sqrt(log(2T)/(epsilon n))}, where T is the data-domain size and n the database size.
The target must hold uniformly over the number and choice of queries.
It would identify the optimal collective accuracy attainable while protecting each database record.
The saved context separates this Euclidean-error question from a maximum-coordinate variant associated with a July 2026 claimed result.
